name: happiness
quote: I got that job I really wanted!
description: An extended experience of pleasure about your situation. It may be triggered by an outcome that significantly improves your life situation or just from recognizing that things are pretty good as they are.
perceptions: An event or realization creates a sense that your situation is good.
results: Happiness ranges in strength from mild to tears of joy.

guidance.description: Consider these articles for tips on how to be happy more often.

variations.name: empathetic happiness
variations.description: Connecting with another person or creature's positive experience that creates a vicarious sense of gaining or fullness.
perceptions: I had a physical or mental interaction with another person or creature who is having a positive experience.
I share a sense of positivity with them.
examples: Your relative has a string of good luck.
A baby bird flies for the first time.

commentaries.quote: It's not necessary for anything to actually change to cause happiness. A shift in perception is enough.

Happiness is not something that you can find, acquire, or achieve directly. You have to get the conditions right and then wait. Some of those conditions are within you, such as coherence among the parts and levels of your personality. Other conditions require relationships to things beyond you: Just as plants need sun, water, and good soil to thrive, people need love, work, and a connection to something larger. It is worth striving to get the right relationships between yourself and others, between yourself and your work, and between yourself and something larger than yourself. If you get these relationships right, a sense of purpose and meaning will emerge.
Happiness is not a goal; it is a by-product.
Happiness is when what you think, what you say, and what you do are in harmony.
